    Abilities

    Abilities are what a power actually does. They go into the abilities field of a Palladium power, and their state decides when they are unlocked and enabled. Every ability that comes with Argon is listed below.

    127 listed · Argon 1.0.0

    Ability Bar

    IDargon:ability_bar
    Holds the data for an ability bar widget. Players fill its slots from an ability pool, with optional presets and crouch variants. Does nothing on its own.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    abilitiesStringList of ability pool entries the player can choose from for each slot.✓/
    slotsInteger (> 0)How many ability bar slots to offer.✗5
    presetsInteger (> 0)How many switchable sets of slot assignments to offer, where 1 disables the preset-switching arrows.✗1
    crouch_variantsBooleanWhether each slot also accepts a separate, crouch-only ability assignment.✗false
    hide_unavailableBooleanHides pool abilities the player can't get yet in the slot picker. Ignores ability_bar_active checks when deciding that.✗true

    {
  "type": "argon:ability_bar",
  "abilities": [
    "argon:example#ability_1",
    "argon:example#ability_2"
  ]
}

    {
  "type": "argon:ability_bar",
  "abilities": [
    {
      "ability": "argon:example#ability_1",
      "slot": 0
    },
    {
      "ability": "argon:example#ability_2",
      "list_index_slot": 0
    }
  ],
  "presets": 3,
  "crouch_variants": true
}

    {
  "name": "Example Power",
  "icon": "minecraft:command_block",
  "abilities": {
    "ability_bar": {
      "type": "argon:ability_bar",
      "abilities": [
        "argon:example#ability_1",
        "argon:example#ability_2"
      ]
    }
  }
}

    Ability Data Attachment Modifier

    IDargon:ability_data_attachment_modifier
    While enabled, watches a list of other abilities. For each enabled one it adds to, subtracts from or sets a shared number data attachment, at its own rate and timer.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    attachmentData Attachment IDThe id of the number-valued data attachment to modify, shared by every entry.✓/
    abilitiesAttachment Modifier,
    Attachment Modifier[]    		Each entry references one of the entity's own abilities (e.g. "fsang:marvel/mutant/cosmic_herald#some_ability"), an operation* ("add" default, "subtract", or "set"), a value used by that operation, and a rate* (default 20 ticks) - the referenced ability's own enabled state is checked every tick, and the modification fires every "rate" ticks it stays enabled.✓/

    abilities (Attachment Modifier)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    abilityAbility ReferenceThe ability whose value is changed.✓/
    operationadd
    subtract
    set    		How the value is applied.✗/
    value(Dynamic) ValueThe amount to add, subtract or set.✓/
    rateInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How often the change is applied.✗/

    {
  "type": "argon:ability_data_attachment_modifier",
  "attachment": "example:my_attachment",
  "abilities": [
    {
      "ability": "example:my_power#some_ability",
      "value": 1
    },
    {
      "ability": "example:my_power#other_ability",
      "operation": "subtract",
      "value": 2,
      "rate": 40
    }
  ]
}

    {
  "name": "Example Power",
  "icon": "minecraft:command_block",
  "abilities": {
    "ability_data_attachment_modifier": {
      "type": "argon:ability_data_attachment_modifier",
      "attachment": "example:my_attachment",
      "abilities": [
        {
          "ability": "example:my_power#some_ability",
          "value": 1
        },
        {
          "ability": "example:my_power#other_ability",
          "operation": "subtract",
          "value": 2,
          "rate": 40
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}

    Anchored Beam

    IDargon:anchored_beam
    While enabled, draws the beam_renderer from a body part, "length" blocks long. Visual only, no aiming or damage. With an animation_timer the beam grows and shrinks.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    beam_rendererIdentifierThe id of the beam renderer whose segments to render in place.✓/
    lengthFloatHow far, in blocks, each segment reaches past its body_part/offset anchor, in the same direction.✗0.5
    rotationVector 3DEuler rotation in degrees (applied X then Y then Z) that tilts which way each segment extends, relative to its own body part's local space - independent of the offset's own direction. E.g. [90, 0, 0] to swing a segment that otherwise hangs straight down (the default with no offset) so it points forward instead, like an upright held tool.✗( 0.000E+0 0.000E+0 0.000E+0)
    yaw_onlyBooleanIf true, the beam only turns with the body's facing and ignores lean, pitch and roll, so it stays level. The start point still follows the body part.✗false

    {
  "type": "argon:anchored_beam",
  "beam_renderer": "example:beam_renderer_id",
  "rotation": [
    90,
    0,
    0
  ]
}

    {
  "name": "Example Power",
  "icon": "minecraft:command_block",
  "abilities": {
    "anchored_beam": {
      "type": "argon:anchored_beam",
      "beam_renderer": "example:beam_renderer_id",
      "rotation": [
        90,
        0,
        0
      ]
    }
  }
}

    Area Burst

    IDargon:area_burst
    On its first enabled tick, hits every living entity in a sphere or cone around the user once with damage, armor penetration, knockback and effects. Can deflect or destroy projectiles. Skips the user, pets, teammates and armor stands.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    shapesphere
    cone    		"sphere" hits everything within the radius. "cone" only hits what is inside cone_angle of where the user looks.✗sphere
    radius(Dynamic) ValueHow far the burst reaches, in blocks.✓/
    cone_angleFloatThe full opening angle of the cone, in degrees.✗60.0
    damage(Dynamic) ValueThe damage dealt to each entity hit.✗/
    damage_typeDamage Type IDThe damage type used; the user's normal attack when left out.✗/
    armor_penetrationFloatThe fraction from 0 to 1 of a hit entity's armor that is ignored.✗0.0
    falloffFloatFrom 0 to 1, how much damage and knockback are reduced for entities at the very edge of the burst.✗0.0
    knockback_distance(Dynamic) ValueHow far, in blocks, hit entities are pushed away from the user. Weakened by knockback resistance.✗/
    lift(Dynamic) ValueUpward launch speed added to the knockback.✗/
    movement_limitMovement LimitScales knockback and lift down for wide entities, as on energy beams.✗/
    effectsBeam Effect[]Mob effects applied to every entity hit.✗/
    projectilesnone
    deflect
    destroy    		"deflect" sends projectiles in range away from the user. "destroy" removes them. The user's own projectiles are left alone.✗none
    hostile_onlyBooleanIf true, only hostile mobs are affected.✗false
    dispelDispelRemoves up to count effects of the given category ("beneficial" or "harmful") from every entity hit, longest first. Bosses are skipped unless skip_bosses is false.✗/
    look_target_rangeDoubleIf set, the burst is centered where the user looks, up to this many blocks away, instead of on the user.✗/
    pushradial
    path_side    		"radial" pushes hit entities straight away from the user. "path_side" pushes them sideways, off the line the user is travelling along, towards the side they are already on.✗radial
    visualsBeam Visual[]Particle visuals spawned at the centre of the burst, in the same format as the visuals of argon:energy_beam, for example a ring.✗[]

    movement_limit (Movement Limit)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    full_below_widthFloat (0.0 ~ 64.0)Targets up to this wide, in blocks, are pushed with full strength.✗1.0
    none_above_widthFloat (0.0 ~ 64.0)Targets at least this wide, in blocks, are not pushed at all. In between, the push fades out.✗3.0
    immovableEntity Type TagEntities in this tag are never pushed.✗/

    effects[] (Beam Effect)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    effectMob Effect IDThe effect to apply.✓/
    durationInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long the effect lasts.✗/
    amplifierInteger (0 ~ 255)The effect level, starting at 0.✗/
    particlesBooleanWhether the effect shows its particles.✗/
    size_tiersSize Tier[]Changes or skips the effect depending on the width or type of the target.✗/

    effects[].size_tiers[] (Size Tier)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    tagEntity Type TagOnly entities in this tag use the tier.✗/
    min_widthDouble (0.0 ~ 64.0)The tier applies to entities at least this wide, in blocks.✗0.0
    skipBooleanIf true, matching entities do not get the effect at all.✗false
    effectMob Effect IDReplaces the effect for matching entities.✗/
    amplifierInteger (0 ~ 255)Replaces the amplifier for matching entities.✗/
    durationInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		Replaces the duration for matching entities.✗/

    dispel (Dispel)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    categorybeneficial
    harmful    		Which category of effects is removed.✗/
    countInteger (1 ~ 64)How many effects are removed at most.✗/
    skip_bossesBooleanIf true, boss mobs are not dispelled.✗/

    visuals[] (Beam Visual)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    shapestreak
    helix
    ring
    sphere
    burst
    crescent    		The particle pattern to draw.✓/
    anchorend
    caster    		Whether the pattern is drawn at the end of the beam or around the caster.✗/
    orientationhorizontal
    vertical    		How ring and crescent patterns are turned.✗/
    particleParticleThe particle used.✓/
    countInteger (1 ~ 512)How many particles the pattern uses.✗/
    radiusFloat (0.0 ~ 64.0)The radius of the pattern in blocks.✗/
    stepFloat (0.05 ~ 16.0)The spacing between particles along the beam.✗/
    pitchFloat (0.1 ~ 64.0)The length of one full twist for helixes, in blocks.✗/
    strandsInteger (1 ~ 8)How many strands a helix has.✗/
    arcFloat (1.0 ~ 360.0)How much of a circle is drawn, in degrees.✗/
    heightFloatThe height of the pattern in blocks.✗/
    ringsInteger (1 ~ 16)How many rings are drawn.✗/
    speedDoubleThe speed of the particles.✗/
    spreadFloat (0.0 ~ 8.0)How far the particles scatter.✗/

    {
  "type": "argon:area_burst",
  "radius": 6,
  "damage": 8
}

    {
  "name": "Example Power",
  "icon": "minecraft:command_block",
  "abilities": {
    "area_burst": {
      "type": "argon:area_burst",
      "radius": 6,
      "damage": 8
    }
  }
}

    Armor Slots (Retrieve)

    IDargon:restore_equipment
    Puts items stored under an ID by the store_equipment ability back into their original slots, then forgets that ID.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    idStringThe ID to restore, matching the one used by the store_equipment ability that stored them.✓/

    {
  "type": "argon:restore_equipment",
  "id": "civilian_clothes"
}

    {
  "name": "Example Power",
  "icon": "minecraft:command_block",
  "abilities": {
    "restore_equipment": {
      "type": "argon:restore_equipment",
      "id": "civilian_clothes"
    }
  }
}

    Armor Slots (Store)

    IDargon:store_equipment
    Stores the items in the given slots under an ID and empties those slots. A matching restore_equipment ability puts them back later.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    idStringThe ID the stored items are saved under.✓/
    slotsmainhand
    offhand
    head
    chest
    legs
    feet
    body
    curios:head
    curios:necklace    		The slots whose items should be stored and cleared.✓/

    {
  "type": "argon:store_equipment",
  "id": "civilian_clothes",
  "slots": [
    "head",
    "chest",
    "legs",
    "feet"
  ]
}

    {
  "name": "Example Power",
  "icon": "minecraft:command_block",
  "abilities": {
    "store_equipment": {
      "type": "argon:store_equipment",
      "id": "civilian_clothes",
      "slots": [
        "head",
        "chest",
        "legs",
        "feet"
      ]
    }
  }
}

    Auto Attack

    IDargon:auto_attack
    While enabled, walks toward the nearest mob in range, jumping over obstacles, and hits it with the held item once it is close enough.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    rangeDoubleHow far from the player a mob can be to be selected as a target and chased.✓/
    attack_rangeDoubleHow close the target needs to be before the player stops moving and attacks it instead.✓/
    speedDoubleThe player's movement speed, in blocks per tick, while chasing a target outside attack range.✓/

    {
  "type": "argon:auto_attack",
  "range": 8,
  "attack_range": 2.5,
  "speed": 0.3
}

    {
  "name": "Example Power",
  "icon": "minecraft:command_block",
  "abilities": {
    "auto_attack": {
      "type": "argon:auto_attack",
      "range": 8,
      "attack_range": 2.5,
      "speed": 0.3
    }
  }
}

    Biome Swap

    IDargon:biome_swap
    While enabled, replaces the terrain within "radius" of where it started with fresh "biome" terrain (optionally in a black concrete shell). Every changed block is restored on disable.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    radiusDoubleHow far from the entity's position (1-64) the swap reaches.✓/
    biomeIdentifierThe biome(s) to generate, vanilla or modded. A single ID, a list of IDs, or a list that mixes IDs with objects that also give a status effect to entities in the area (see the second example).✓/
    height_belowIntegerHow many blocks below the entity's feet are included when sphere is false.✗4
    height_aboveIntegerHow many blocks above the entity's feet are included when sphere is false.✗4
    sphereBooleanIf true, the area is a full sphere inside a solid black concrete shell instead of a column limited by radius.✗false
    unbreakableBooleanIf true, none of the newly added blocks can be broken while the ability is enabled.✗true
    build_animationBooleanIf true, the area grows in and shrinks out over a couple of seconds instead of popping in and out.✗true

    {
  "type": "argon:biome_swap",
  "radius": 10,
  "biome": "minecraft:desert"
}

    {
  "type": "argon:biome_swap",
  "radius": 16,
  "biome": [
    {
      "biome": "minecraft:crimson_forest",
      "effect": "minecraft:fire_resistance",
      "amplifier": 1,
      "affect_self": false
    },
    "minecraft:deep_dark"
  ],
  "height_below": 6,
  "height_above": 8,
  "sphere": true,
  "unbreakable": false,
  "build_animation": false
}

    {
  "name": "Example Power",
  "icon": "minecraft:command_block",
  "abilities": {
    "biome_swap": {
      "type": "argon:biome_swap",
      "radius": 10,
      "biome": "minecraft:desert"
    }
  }
}

    Blast Chain

    IDargon:blast_chain
    Fires a beam that only damages on reaching its target. If it hits a living entity it fires on to the nearest other visible living entity, up to "chain_count" more times.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    beam_rendererIdentifierThe id of the beam renderer to use for every segment of the chain.✓/
    damageFloatThe damage dealt to the entity hit by the initial shot.✗0.0
    damage_falloffFloatMultiplier on "damage" for each jump already taken (0.85 means the 2nd hit deals 85%, the 3rd 72.25%). 1 means no falloff. Effects keep their full strength.✗1.0
    max_distanceFloatThe maximum distance the initial shot can travel before giving up.✗30.0
    speedFloatThe blocks every beam piece (initial shot and every chain jump) travels per tick.✗2.0
    lengthFloatThe length of the traveling beam piece, in blocks.✗4.0
    set_on_fire_ticksIntegerHow many ticks each hit entity is set on fire for.✗0
    cause_fireBooleanIf the initial shot should ignite flammable blocks it hits instead of a living entity.✗false
    smelt_blocksBooleanIf the initial shot should smelt the block it hits instead of a living entity.✗false
    chain_countInteger (>= 0)The maximum number of additional jumps after the initial hit.✗3
    chain_rangeFloatHow far, in blocks, from each impact point to search for the next chain target.✗8.0
    can_hit_casterBooleanWhether a jump can pick the caster as its next target. The first shot never hits the caster.✗false
    effectsPotion Hit Effect,
    Potion Hit Effect[]    		Applied, at full configured strength, to every entity hit by the chain (the initial hit and every jump). Same entry format as "potion_hit"'s "effects": effect, duration, amplifier, max_amplifier and particles*.✗[]
    damage_typeDamage Type IDA damage type ID such as "minecraft:magic" or one from a pack. Left unset, it is a player attack when a player uses this and a mob attack otherwise. Unknown types fall back to that.✗/

    effects (Potion Hit Effect)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    effectMob Effect IDThe effect to apply.✓/
    durationInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long the effect lasts.✓/
    amplifierIntegerThe effect level, starting at 0.✗/
    max_amplifierIntegerThe highest level repeated hits can stack the effect up to.✗/
    particlesBooleanWhether the effect shows its particles.✗/

    {
  "type": "argon:blast_chain",
  "beam_renderer": "example:beam_renderer_id",
  "damage": 6,
  "damage_falloff": 0.85,
  "max_distance": 25,
  "speed": 2.5,
  "effects": {
    "effect": "minecraft:poison",
    "duration": 60,
    "max_amplifier": 3
  }
}

    {
  "name": "Example Power",
  "icon": "minecraft:command_block",
  "abilities": {
    "blast_chain": {
      "type": "argon:blast_chain",
      "beam_renderer": "example:beam_renderer_id",
      "damage": 6,
      "damage_falloff": 0.85,
      "max_distance": 25,
      "speed": 2.5,
      "effects": {
        "effect": "minecraft:poison",
        "duration": 60,
        "max_amplifier": 3
      }
    }
  }
}

    Blink

    IDargon:blink
    On activation, teleports you up to "distance" blocks along your look direction. Stops before solid blocks, and can pass through see-through ones like glass ("allow_see_through").

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    distance(Dynamic) ValueThe maximum distance, in blocks, the user is teleported.✓/
    allow_see_throughBooleanWhether see-through solid blocks (glass etc.) are passed through instead of stopping the teleport.✗true
    safeBooleanIf true, the blink fails (nothing happens) when the destination is inside blocks, in or over lava, fire or magma, cactus, or over the void.✗false
    respect_protectionBooleanIf true, the blink fails when a player user could not interact with the destination blocks (spawn protection, claim mods).✗false
    particlesParticle Effect[]Optional particle effects played at the user's start and end positions in list order, skipped if the user doesn't actually move, where each entry is a full particle options object with an optional world-space offset.✗[]

    particles[] (Particle Effect)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    particleParticleThe particle to spawn.✓/
    countInteger (>= 0)How many particles spawn.✗/
    spreadDoubleHow far the particles spread from the origin.✗/
    speedDoubleThe speed of the particles.✗/
    offsetVector 3DOffset from the origin in blocks.✗/

    {
  "type": "argon:blink",
  "distance": 20,
  "properties": {

    Block Energy

    IDargon:block_energy
    While enabled, drains RF from or adds RF to the block you look at, every tick, as long as it is within range and exposes an energy storage. With an energy_bar the drained RF fills that bar and added RF is taken from it, otherwise the RF is simply removed from or created in the block.

    modeString"drain" pulls RF out of the block, "add" pushes RF into it, "toggle" adds while the user is sneaking and drains otherwise.✗drain
    range(Dynamic) ValueHow far away, in blocks, the block can be.✗8
    rate(Dynamic) ValueThe most RF moved per tick.✗100
    energy_barStringAn energy bar, as "power#bar_name". Drained RF fills it and added RF is spent from it. Left unset, no bar is used and the energy is unlimited.✗/

    Calm

    IDargon:calm
    While enabled, looking at an eligible mob long enough calms it. It gets a calm effect and a lockout effect that stops it being calmed again for a while. Owned, already calmed or locked out mobs are skipped.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    rangeDoubleHow far away the mob can be, in blocks.✗6.0
    hold_timeInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long the user has to keep looking at the same mob.✗60
    entity_tagEntity Type ID(s) / TagOnly mobs in this tag can be calmed. Leave it out to allow every mob.✗/
    excluded_tagsEntity Type ID(s) / TagMobs in any of these tags can never be calmed.✗/
    calm_effectMob Effect IDThe effect that calms the mob.✗argon:calmed
    calm_durationInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long the calm effect lasts.✗400
    lockout_effectMob Effect IDThe effect that stops the mob from being calmed again.✗argon:calm_lockout
    lockout_durationInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long the lockout lasts.✗1200

    Carry

    IDargon:carry
    While enabled, grabs the living entity you look at and holds it on a damped spring at an attachment point. It lags and swings as you move but never goes past "maximum_distance". Disabling lets go.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    rangeDoubleHow far away, in blocks, a target can be grabbed from.✓/
    attachmentVector 3D,
    right_shoulder
    left_shoulder
    right_hand
    left_hand
    chest
    above_head
    main_hand
    off_hand
    main_shoulder
    off_shoulder    		Where the carried entity is drawn toward, in the wearer's frame (x right, y up from the feet, z forward): an [x, y, z] offset, or right_shoulder, left_shoulder, right_hand, left_hand, chest, above_head, or main/off_hand and main/off_shoulder by the wearer's main arm.✗right_shoulder
    preferred_distanceDoubleRadius around the attachment point inside which the target is held only loosely.✗0.6
    maximum_distanceDoubleRadius around the attachment point the target can never leave (a wall can still push it past this).✗1.5
    stiffnessDoubleSpring strength pulling the target to the attachment point.✗0.2
    dampingDoubleHow strongly the target's motion relative to you is resisted. Higher settles faster, lower swings longer.✗0.5
    gravity_influenceDoubleHow much normal gravity acts on the target, so it hangs below you when not pulled up. 0 is none, 1 is full.✗1.0
    inertiaDoubleThe target's mass. Spring and damping are divided by it, so higher means more lag and swing.✗1.0
    follow_strengthDoubleHow much of each change in your velocity is passed straight to the target. 0 means only the spring moves it, 1 means it follows exactly.✗0.35
    acquire_ticksIntegerMost ticks the initial pull-in lasts before normal carry physics takes over.✗6
    target_collisionBooleanWhether the carried entity is kept out of walls. If a block is in the way it is pulled back along the line from you instead of going through it.✗true
    preserve_release_velocityBooleanWhether the target keeps its velocity when let go, rather than stopping dead.✗true
    allow_mobsBooleanWhether non-player entities can be grabbed.✗true
    allow_playersBooleanWhether players can be grabbed.✗false
    visual_tiltDoubleHow much the carried entity pitches and rolls with the sway when drawn. 0 keeps it upright, 1 is as calculated, higher exaggerates, negative tilts the other way.✗1.0
    arm_poseBooleanWhether your arm on the attachment side aims at the carried entity automatically (both arms for a centered attachment). Turn it off to animate the arms yourself with the argon.carry_* queries.✗true
    safe_releaseBooleanWhether the released entity takes no fall damage from its next fall.✗false
    excluded_tagsEntity Type ID(s) / TagEntity types in any of these tags can never be grabbed, for example #c:bosses.✗/
    max_widthDoubleEntities wider than this many blocks can't be grabbed. 0 means no limit.✗0.0
    max_heightDoubleEntities taller than this many blocks can't be grabbed. 0 means no limit.✗0.0
    max_healthDoubleEntities with more max health than this can't be grabbed. 0 means no limit.✗0.0
    max_durationIntegerThe carry lets go on its own after this many ticks. 0 means no limit.✗0
    player_duration_multiplierDoubleMultiplies max_duration when the carried entity is a player, so players can be held for a shorter time.✗1.0

    Collision Attack

    IDargon:collision_attack
    While enabled and moving faster than "min_speed", every living entity the user runs into takes damage and is knocked away along the user's direction of travel. Damage and knockback grow with how far the speed is above "min_speed". Each target can only be hit again after "hit_cooldown" ticks. Allied entities, the user's vehicle and passengers are skipped.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    min_speedDoubleHorizontal speed in blocks per second the user has to exceed before anything is hit.✗20.0
    damageDoubleDamage dealt at exactly min_speed.✗4.0
    damage_per_speedDoubleExtra damage for every block per second above min_speed.✗0.25
    knockbackDoubleKnockback strength at exactly min_speed.✗0.8
    knockback_per_speedDoubleExtra knockback strength for every block per second above min_speed.✗0.03
    upward_knockbackDoubleUpward velocity added to the target when it is hit.✗0.3
    inflationDoubleHow much the user's hitbox is grown, in blocks, when looking for entities to hit. The box is also stretched along the distance moved this tick so fast runs cannot skip over targets.✗0.4
    hit_cooldownIntegerTicks before the same target can be hit again.✗20
    affect_playersBooleanIf false, other players are never hit.✗true
    excluded_entitiesIdentifier[]Entity types that are never hit, so the run passes straight through them. Defaults to minecraft:armor_stand and palladium:suit_stand.✗/
    hit_effectsPotion Hit Effect,
    Potion Hit Effect[]    		Effects applied to every target that is hit, for example bleeding.✗[]
    effects_min_speedDoubleHorizontal speed in blocks per second the user has to reach before hit_effects, hit_visuals and hit_sound are used. Slower hits only do damage.✗0.0
    hit_visualsBeam Visual[]Particle visuals spawned at every target that is hit, in the same format as the visuals of argon:energy_beam.✗[]
    visuals_require_bloodBooleanIf true, hit_visuals are skipped for entities in the argon:bloodless tag, so blood particles do not appear on things that cannot bleed.✗false
    hit_soundIdentifierA sound event played at every target that is hit, instead of the default hit sound.✗/
    hit_sound_volumeFloatVolume of hit_sound.✗1.0
    hit_sound_pitchFloatPitch of hit_sound.✗0.9

    hit_effects (Potion Hit Effect)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    effectMob Effect IDThe effect to apply.✓/
    durationInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long the effect lasts.✓/
    amplifierIntegerThe effect level, starting at 0.✗/
    max_amplifierIntegerThe highest level repeated hits can stack the effect up to.✗/
    particlesBooleanWhether the effect shows its particles.✗/

    hit_visuals[] (Beam Visual)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    shapestreak
    helix
    ring
    sphere
    burst
    crescent    		The particle pattern to draw.✓/
    anchorend
    caster    		Whether the pattern is drawn at the end of the beam or around the caster.✗/
    orientationhorizontal
    vertical    		How ring and crescent patterns are turned.✗/
    particleParticleThe particle used.✓/
    countInteger (1 ~ 512)How many particles the pattern uses.✗/
    radiusFloat (0.0 ~ 64.0)The radius of the pattern in blocks.✗/
    stepFloat (0.05 ~ 16.0)The spacing between particles along the beam.✗/
    pitchFloat (0.1 ~ 64.0)The length of one full twist for helixes, in blocks.✗/
    strandsInteger (1 ~ 8)How many strands a helix has.✗/
    arcFloat (1.0 ~ 360.0)How much of a circle is drawn, in degrees.✗/
    heightFloatThe height of the pattern in blocks.✗/
    ringsInteger (1 ~ 16)How many rings are drawn.✗/
    speedDoubleThe speed of the particles.✗/

    Color Cycle Glow

    IDargon:color_cycle_glow
    While enabled, gives the entity an outline that cycles through "colors" in order. It follows world time so everyone sees the same color. Independent of entity_glow and the Glowing effect. By default it is visible through walls, and the outline is a solid colour, so "intensity" dims it towards black.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    colorsColor[]The ordered list of colors to cycle through and fade between; must contain at least one color.✓/
    rateInteger (> 0)How many ticks (20 per second) each fade from one color to the next takes.✗20
    intensityFloat / Value(Dynamic) 0 to 1, how strong the outline is. The outline is always opaque, so this mixes the colour from faded_color (at 0) to the cycling colour (at 1), for example from an argon:power_age value.✗1.0
    faded_colorColorThe colour the outline mixes towards as intensity drops to 0, black by default.✗#000000
    through_wallsBooleanIf false, the outline is only shown to viewers who have a clear line of sight to the entity, so it disappears behind blocks.✗true

    Damage Reaction

    IDargon:damage_reaction
    While enabled, the first reaction matching an incoming hit changes it. It can scale or cancel damage, cancel knockback, hit the attacker back, give effects, and cut another ability's cooldown. argon:reacted can check the last reaction.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    reactionsDamage Reaction[]Checked in order, the first match wins. kind is "any", "melee" or "projectile"; min_damage is the smallest hit it applies to; damage_multiplier is how much of the damage still goes through (0 cancels the hit); counter_damage is a Value dealt back to a living attacker; attacker_effects and self_effects are lists of { effect, duration, amplifier, particles }; cooldown_cap is { ability, cap* } and lowers that key bind ability's remaining cooldown to at most cap.✓/

    reactions[] (Damage Reaction)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    idStringA name for the reaction.✗/
    kindany
    melee
    projectile    		Which kind of damage triggers the reaction.✗/
    min_damageFloat (>= 0.0)The damage has to be at least this much.✗0.0
    damage_multiplierFloat (0.0 ~ 1.0)Multiplies the damage taken.✗/
    cancel_knockbackBooleanWhether the knockback is cancelled.✗/
    counter_damage(Dynamic) ValueDamage dealt back to the attacker.✗/
    attacker_effectsBeam Effect[]Effects applied to the attacker.✗/
    self_effectsBeam Effect[]Effects applied to the user.✗/
    cooldown_capCooldown CapCuts down the cooldown of another ability.✗/

    reactions[].attacker_effects[] (Beam Effect)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    effectMob Effect IDThe effect to apply.✓/
    durationInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long the effect lasts.✗/
    amplifierInteger (0 ~ 255)The effect level, starting at 0.✗/
    particlesBooleanWhether the effect shows its particles.✗/
    size_tiersSize Tier[]Changes or skips the effect depending on the width or type of the target.✗/

    reactions[].attacker_effects[].size_tiers[] (Size Tier)

    Energy Beam

    IDargon:energy_beam
    Shoots a beam that can bounce off blocks. On hitting a matching entity it can redirect onward or spread into several beams once. Applies damage, fire and smelting along its path.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    beam_rendererIdentifierThe id of the beam renderer to use.✓/
    damage(Dynamic) ValueDamage dealt to every entity the beam hits. A value, so it can follow a data attachment to scale with a level.✗0
    max_distance(Dynamic) ValueTotal distance the beam can travel across all its bounces. A value, so it can follow a data attachment to scale with a level.✗30
    max_bouncesInteger (>= 0)Most times the beam can bounce off blocks or entities (a spread counts as one) before stopping at its next hit.✗4
    set_on_fire_ticksIntegerHow many ticks the beam sets a hit entity on fire for.✗0
    cause_fireBooleanWhether the beam ignites flammable blocks it touches.✗false
    smelt_blocksBooleanWhether the beam smelts every block it touches.✗false
    redirect_off_blocksBooleanWhether the beam bounces off blocks instead of stopping at them. When false, only 'entity_reaction' can redirect it.✗true
    entity_reactionnone
    redirect
    spread    		What happens when the beam hits an entity matching 'entity_bounce_condition': continue, redirect, or spread into multiple beams.✗NONE
    entity_bounce_conditionCondition,
    Condition[]    		A condition limiting which hit entities can redirect or spread the beam. Ignored when 'entity_reaction' is 'none', otherwise defaults to all entities.✗/
    spread_countInteger (> 0)Number of beams the spread effect bursts into when 'entity_reaction' is 'spread'.✗5
    spread_angleFloatAngle in degrees the spread beams fan out from the central reflected direction when 'entity_reaction' is 'spread'.✗25.0
    coneConeMakes damage, fire, smelting and block mode reach across a cone instead of a line. Widths in blocks at the eyes ("start_size", 0.1) and at "end_distance" (default "max_distance"); "rays" (1-128, default 24) finds blocks. Pair with the argon:cone renderer.✗/
    knockback(Dynamic) ValueHow hard the beam pushes living entities away from the caster. 1 is firm, 5 is a gale, 0 is none. Knockback resistance weakens it. A value, so it can follow a data attachment to scale with a level.✗0
    knockback_ignores_resistanceBooleanWhether "knockback" ignores the target's knockback resistance.✗false
    block_modeBlock ModeWhat the beam does to blocks it hits: "type" is "melt" or "freeze", with "time" (default 60 ticks), "auto_time", "speed_multiplier", "modifiers", "conversions" and "particle"; freeze adds "frozen_time", "slippery", "friction" and "snow_layers". See the examples.✗/
    chargeBeam ChargeTurns the beam into a charged shot: hold the ability to charge and release to fire. Releasing before "min_time" (default 10) fires nothing and the charge is full at "max_time" (default 40), eased by "curve" (linear, ease_in, ease_out, ease_in_out). The beam then shows for "fire_time" (default 8), and with a "taper" from 0 to 1 it appears at full length and narrows to nothing over that fraction of the end of that time instead of retracting, and "grow" (default 0.15) is the fraction of the start over which it widens from nothing to full size. "shots" (default 1) fires that many shots "shot_interval" ticks apart (default 4), each aimed where you look at that moment, and "ignore_hit_immunity" lets every shot damage the same target. Each of the other settings is a { min, max } range used for damage, range, knockback and the amplifier and duration of the entity effects, from no charge to full charge. See the charged beam example.✗/
    pierceBooleanWhether the beam passes through every entity in its way and hits all of them, stopping only at a block or its max_distance.✗false
    pierce_limitInteger (>= 0)With pierce, the most entities the beam passes through: it ends at the last one. 0 is no limit.✗0
    pierce_full_charge_onlyBooleanWith pierce and a charge, only a fully charged shot passes through entities; weaker shots stop at the first one.✗false
    pierce_sizePierce SizeWith pierce, how far in blocks the beam's reach extends sideways (width) and up and down (height) around the line, so a wide flat or tall thin slash can hit entities beside its path. Default 0.3 for both.✗/
    knockback_distance(Dynamic) ValueHow far, in blocks, hit living entities are launched away from the caster (or the impact point), instead of the "knockback" strength. Knockback resistance weakens it.✗/
    lift(Dynamic) ValueUpward launch speed added by "knockback_distance" (0.4 is roughly a block and a half).✗/
    airborne_lift(Dynamic) ValueUpward launch speed used instead of "lift" while the caster is not on the ground.✗/
    lateral_pull(Dynamic) ValueHow far, in blocks, hit living entities are pulled sideways across the look direction toward the aim line, on top of any knockback. Knockback resistance weakens it.✗/
    armor_penetrationFloatThe fraction from 0 to 1 of a hit entity's armor ignored by the damage.✗0.0
    heavy_armorHeavy ArmorAdds "bonus" damage to hit entities whose armor value is at least "threshold".✗/
    impactImpactMakes the beam burst where it ends: every living entity within "radius" blocks of that point is hit instead of the entities on the line, launched away from the point, with damage reduced by up to "falloff" (0 to 1) at the edge.✗/
    visualsBeam Visual[]Particle effects spawned when the beam fires, for beams that should look like air or smoke instead of a laser. "shape" is "streak" (particles along the beam every "step" blocks with "spread" jitter), "helix" ("strands" spirals of "radius" and "pitch" along the beam), "ring" ("rings" rings up to "radius" with "count" particles each, only "arc" degrees facing forward if under 360), "sphere" ("count" particles on a sphere of "radius") or "burst" (the same, filled). "crescent" draws crescent-shaped arcs of "count" particles along the beam every "step" blocks, spanning "arc" degrees (150 by default), sideways or up and down by "orientation" ("horizontal" or "vertical"). "anchor" is "end" (where the beam ends, default) or "caster" for rings, "height" raises them, and "speed" sends the particles along the beam or outward.✗/
    entity_effectsBeam Effect[]Mob effects given to every living entity the beam hits. Duration is ticks or a time like "5s" (default 5s), amplifier 0 is level one, particles defaults to false.✗/
    damage_typeDamage Type IDDamage type ID the damage is dealt as. Unset, it is a player attack for players and a mob attack otherwise.✗/
    damage_type_overridesDamage Type Override[]Damage types used instead of "damage_type" while their condition is true. Checked in order, first match wins. See the damage type overrides example.✗[]

    cone (Cone)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    start_sizeFloat (0.0 ~ 64.0)The width of the cone at the origin, in blocks.✗/
    end_sizeFloat (0.0 ~ 64.0)The width of the cone at its far end, in blocks.✗/

    value(Dynamic) ValueThe amount used by "operation", evaluated fresh every time the ability modifies the item.✓/
    rateInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long to wait between modifications.✗20

    attach_to_entityBooleanIf true, hitting a living entity within range pulls it toward the caster.✗true
    attach_to_blockBooleanIf true, hitting a block within range pulls the caster toward it.✗true
    speedDoubleThe velocity, in blocks/tick, that the pulled entity (or the caster) moves at.✓/
    beam_rendererIdentifierThe beam renderer id used to draw the rope (e.g. a custom one under data//palladium/beams/).✓/
    effectsBeam Effect[]Mob effects applied to a living entity when the grapple hits it.✗/

    Ground Beam

    IDargon:ground_beam
    While enabled, draws damaging ground beams under entities with solid ground within "max_ground_depth" blocks. "mode" "area" (default) hits every other living entity within "range", "target" only the one you look at.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    beam_rendererIdentifierThe id of the beam renderer to use for each ground-to-target beam.✓/
    rangeDoubleIn "area" mode, how far from the user, in blocks, to search for targets. In "target" mode, the farthest a target can be while you look at it.✓/
    modearea
    target    		Whether this affects every qualifying entity within "range" of the user ("area") or only the single qualifying entity the user is currently looking at ("target").✗area
    max_ground_depthDoubleHow far, in blocks, to search straight down from a target for solid ground. A target with no ground in that depth gets no beam and takes no damage that tick.✗64.0
    damageFloatDamage dealt to every beamed entity every "damage_rate" ticks. Leave at 0 for a cosmetic beam.✗0.0
    damage_rateInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long, in ticks, to wait between damage applications.✗20
    no_knockbackBooleanIf true, damaged entities are not knocked back.✗false
    powersPower Requirement,
    Power Requirement[]    		Restricts which entities can be targeted based on the powers they hold. Each entry lists a "power" (an explicit power id, a power tag ("#namespace:tag"), or a mix of both) and an optional "mode" - "include" (default) requires at least one matching power to be present, "exclude" requires all of them to be absent; an entity only counts if it satisfies every entry. Leave unset (the default) to target all living entities in range.✗/
    damage_typeDamage Type IDA damage type ID such as "minecraft:magic" or one from a pack. Left unset, it is a player attack when a player uses this and a mob attack otherwise. Unknown types fall back to that.✗/

    powers (Power Requirement)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    powerPower ID(s) / TagThe power or powers the entity has to have.✓/
    modeinclude
    exclude    		Whether the entity must have the power (include) or must not have it (exclude).✗include

  "type": "argon:ground_beam",
  "beam_renderer": "example:beam_renderer_id",
  "range": 10,
  "damage": 2,
  "no_knockback": true
}

  "range": 10,
  "damage": 2,
  "powers": [
    {
      "power": "example:ally_power",
      "mode": "exclude"
    }
  ]
}

    Hearing

    IDargon:hearing
    Client only. Labels each sound you hear with its subtitle and pins it in the world until it fades. Sounds beyond their normal range are forwarded up to "range" blocks as silent markers.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    range(Dynamic) ValueThe farthest a sound can be from the holder, in blocks, and still show. Includes sounds the server forwards from beyond their normal distance. Capped at 512 for forwarded sounds.✗32.0
    durationInteger (1 ~ 12000)How long a sound's marker lasts before it is gone. It stays fully visible for the first 60% and fades over the rest.✗100
    max_markersInteger (1 ~ 512)The most markers shown at once; the oldest are dropped first.✗64
    include_unlabeledBooleanWhether sounds with no subtitle in the game's sound definitions are shown too, labeled with the sound's own id.✗false
    see_throughBooleanWhether markers are visible through blocks.✗true
    ignore_ownBooleanWhether sounds made at the holder's own position (their footsteps, their hurt sound) are skipped.✗true
    scaleFloat (0.1 ~ 8.0)Size multiplier for the marker text.✗1.0
    colorColorThe text color, white by default.✗/
    exclude_sourcesstring[]Sound categories that are never shown: any of master, music, record, weather, block, hostile, neutral, player, ambient, voice, ui. Sounds not placed in the world (interface sounds) are always skipped.✗[ "master", "music", "record", "ui" ]
    muffle_footstepsBooleanWhether footsteps on a soft surface can't be heard. A step is skipped when the block the walker stands in or on is one of the "muffling_blocks". The server applies the same rule to sounds it forwards from far away.✗true
    muffling_blocksBlock ID(s) / TagThe blocks that muffle footsteps when "muffle_footsteps" is on, given as explicit block IDs, a tag ("#namespace:tag"), or a mix of both. Left unset, it is vanilla's "#minecraft:dampens_vibrations" tag, which is wool and carpets.✗/
    hostile_colorColorText color for sounds made by hostile mobs, instead of "color".✗/
    player_colorColorText color for sounds made by players, instead of "color".✗/
    neutral_colorColorText color for sounds made by neutral and passive mobs, instead of "color".✗/
    prioritizeBooleanWhen more sounds are heard than "max_markers" allows, drop the least significant (ambient and block sounds first, then far-away ones) instead of the oldest. Hostile and player sounds rank highest.✗false
    edge_arrowsBooleanShows a small pointer on the edge of the screen for every marker that is outside your view, pointing the way to the sound.✗false

    {
  "type": "argon:hearing",
  "range": 48,
  "duration": 120,
  "color": "#FFFFFF",
  "exclude_sources": [
    "master",
    "music",
    "record",
    "ui"
  ]
}

      ]
    }
  }

    Held Target

    IDargon:held_target
    Deals damage, applies effects and knocks back the entity the user holds with argon:carry (or let go of in the last few ticks). Each entry runs on the first tick, every tick, or the last tick. Does nothing when nothing is held.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    applicationsHeld Application[]What to do to the held target. timing is "first_tick", "tick" or "last_tick"; interval is how often a "tick" entry runs; damage is a Value; armor_penetration is the fraction from 0 to 1 of the target's armor ignored by the damage; damage_type is a damage type ID (unset, a player attack); effects is a list of { effect*, duration, amplifier, particles }; knockback_distance (Value, blocks, away from the user) and lift (Value, upward speed) are weakened by knockback resistance; reset_invulnerability (default false) clears the target's hit immunity just before the damage so several quick hits all land.✓/
    release_windowIntegerHow many ticks after the target was let go it still counts as held, so an entry can run on the tick the carry ends.✗6

    applications[] (Held Application)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    timingfirst_tick
    tick
    last_tick    		When the application happens while the ability is held.✓/
    intervalInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		The delay between applications when the timing is tick.✗/
    damage(Dynamic) ValueThe damage dealt.✗/
    armor_penetrationFloat (0.0 ~ 1.0)How much of the target's armor is ignored.✗/
    damage_typeDamage Type IDThe damage type used.✗/
    effectsBeam Effect[]Effects applied to the target.✗/
    knockback_distance(Dynamic) ValueHow far the target is knocked back.✗/
    lift(Dynamic) ValueHow much the target is lifted.✗/
    reset_invulnerabilityBooleanWhether the target's invulnerability frames are reset so the hit lands.✗/

    applications[].effects[] (Beam Effect)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    effectMob Effect IDThe effect to apply.✓/
    durationInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long the effect lasts.✗/
    amplifierInteger (0 ~ 255)The effect level, starting at 0.✗/
    particlesBooleanWhether the effect shows its particles.✗/
    size_tiersSize Tier[]Changes or skips the effect depending on the width or type of the target.✗/

    applications[].effects[].size_tiers[] (Size Tier)

    tagEntity Type TagOnly entities in this tag use the tier.✗/

    Highlight

    IDargon:highlight
    Client only. Tints the entity's model (and optionally matching blocks in range) with a color, visible through walls to the ability holder only.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    modeself
    others    		Whether this ability highlights the entity itself or lets you see other entities (self, others). Seeing others also needs "highlight_entities".✗SELF
    colorColorThe highlight color, defaulting to the team color for entities or white for blocks when unset.✗/
    opacityFloat (0.0 ~ 1.0)How strong the tint is, from 0 (invisible) to 1 (fully opaque).✗0.1
    distance(Dynamic) ValueThe distance at which entities (in "others" mode) and enabled matching blocks are highlighted.✗0
    styletint
    outline    		How highlighted entities are drawn: tint fills the model with the color, outline draws the vanilla glow outline in the color (works on invisible entities too, and the opacity does not apply).✗TINT
    highlight_entitiesBooleanIf true, "others" mode also highlights entities within "distance" through walls. Off by default, so "others" only shows blocks. No effect in "self" mode.✗false
    entitiesEntity Type ID(s) / TagThe entity types to highlight when "highlight_entities" is true, given as explicit entity type IDs, a tag ("#namespace:tag"), or a mix of both. Left unset, every living entity in range is highlighted.✗/
    highlight_blocksBooleanIf true, also highlights every block matching "blocks" within "distance", through walls.✗false
    blocksBlock ID(s) / TagThe blocks to highlight when "highlight_blocks" is true, given as explicit block IDs, a tag ("#namespace:tag"), or a mix of both.✗/
    blocked_byBlock ID(s) / TagBlock types that still block line of sight for this effect, hiding anything behind them while everything else stays visible through walls.✗/
    hostile_colorColorHighlight color for hostile mobs (and neutral ones targeting the holder). When any of the four category colors is set, each highlighted entity uses the color of its category instead of "color"; categories without a color fall back to "color".✗/
    ally_colorColorHighlight color for allies: the holder's team members, owned pets, and entities allied through vanilla teams.✗/
    neutral_colorColorHighlight color for everything else that is not hostile, a player or an ally (animals, villagers, passive mobs).✗/
    player_colorColorHighlight color for players who are not allies.✗/

    Hunger Rate

    IDargon:hunger_rate
    While enabled, scales how fast a player's hunger drains and how much food and saturation they gain back. 100 is vanilla. 50 for drain means hunger drops half as fast, 50 for refill means food only restores half as much hunger and saturation (the fractions carry over, so two food points still add up). Values above 100 speed things up. Several enabled instances multiply their drain.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    drain_percentIntegerPercent of the normal exhaustion the player takes from moving, jumping, fighting and regenerating. 0 stops hunger from draining.✗100
    refill_percentIntegerPercent of the normal food level and saturation the player gets back whenever either increases.✗100

  }
}

      }
    }
  }
}

    palladium.ability.argon.throwable_item

    IDargon:throwable_item
    Throws the configured item from the holder's hand as a physical projectile that looks like the item, keeping its exact ItemStack (components, enchantments, durability) in a saved server record so it can never be duplicated or lost. Activating the ability again while the item is out recalls it (when recall_enabled). The projectile can bounce or embed in blocks, damage and pass through entities, return on its own after configured triggers, hit things on the way back, and be caught by its owner. Almost every number is a Value, so power progression can change it between throws. Values are read when the item is thrown, except the return_* settings and catch_radius, which are read again when the item is recalled. The item is restored to its original slot (or the inventory, or the ground) when caught, picked up, or when the owner logs out, dies or changes dimension.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    itemItem ID(s) / TagThe item, items or #tag the ability can throw, e.g. "fsang:mjolnir" or ["minecraft:diamond_sword"].✓/
    handmain_hand
    off_hand
    either    		Which hand to take the item from.✗main_hand
    pickupThrowable PickupWhether and how the owner picks the item up again.✗/
    throwThrow SettingsHow the item is thrown and how far it can fly.✗/
    combatThrow CombatWhat the item does to entities it hits.✗/
    block_impactThrow Block ImpactWhat the item does when it hits a block.✗/
    returnThrow ReturnHow and when the item comes back to its owner.✗/
    renderThrow RenderHow the thrown item looks.✗/
    soundsThrow SoundsSounds for each stage of the throw. All are optional sound ids from sounds.json.✗/
    targetingThrow TargetingHow the item picks a target.✗/
    homingThrow HomingHow the item steers towards its target.✗/
    ricochetThrow RicochetLets the item jump to further targets after a hit.✗/
    steeringThrow SteeringLets the owner steer the item in flight while an argon:throw_steer ability is held.✗/
    cameraThrow CameraThe camera used when the steering mode is projectile_camera.✗/
    perfect_catchThrow Perfect CatchA bonus for catching the item at the right moment.✗/
    pinThrow PinPins a hit entity to a wall behind it.✗/
    deflectionThrow DeflectionLets the item knock projectiles aside while it flies.✗/

    Path Vision

    IDargon:path_vision
    Client only. Shows where nearby entities and projectiles are heading: a mob's AI route, a short prediction for other movers, a projectile's predicted flight. Drawn as a trail, changes nothing.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    detection_radiusDouble (1.0 ~ 256.0)How far from the holder, in blocks, entities and projectiles are looked for. Only loaded entities are ever considered.✗24.0
    max_targetsInteger (1 ~ 128)The most targets shown at once. Which ones are kept when there are more is decided by target_priority.✗16
    target_priorityclosest
    hostile_first
    projectiles_first    		Which targets are kept when more than max_targets are in range and which come first: "closest" orders by distance, "hostile_first" puts hostile mobs before everything else, "projectiles_first" puts projectiles first. Within a group the closest come first.✗closest
    path_update_intervalInteger (1 ~ 40)How often paths are recalculated. Between updates the trail follows the target smoothly, and a new navigation path from the server updates it immediately.✗2
    max_path_lengthDouble (1.0 ~ 512.0)The longest stretch of path shown, measured along the path itself from the target.✗32.0
    trackstring[]What is shown, mixing categories ("players", "hostile", "passive", "neutral", "projectiles", "mobs", "all") with entity type ids and "#tags". Listed types and tags are tracked whatever their category. An unknown entry stops the power from loading.✗[ "players", "hostile", "neutral", "projectiles" ]
    ignorestring[]Anything that matches here is never shown, even when it matches track. Takes the same entries as track.✗[]
    show_entity_pathsBooleanWhether paths are shown for mobs and players.✗true
    predict_entity_movementBooleanWhether an entity with no active path gets a physics prediction from its recent velocity. It is an estimate, not a destination, and assumes the entity keeps going the way it is going.✗true
    entity_prediction_timeDouble (0.1 ~ 10.0)How far ahead entity movement is predicted. Longer predictions get less reliable.✗2.0
    show_projectile_pathsBooleanWhether the flight of projectiles is shown.✗true
    projectile_prediction_timeDouble (0.1 ~ 10.0)How far ahead a projectile's flight is simulated. The path also stops at the first expected collision.✗3.0
    show_projectile_impactBooleanWhether a particle marks where a projectile is expected to hit. Nothing shows when no impact is predicted.✗true
    show_time_to_impactBooleanWhether the time left before the predicted impact is written above the impact point, such as 0.8s.✗false
    impact_particleParticleThe particle that marks the predicted impact, as a particle type ID or a particle object.✗minecraft:end_rod
    preview_aimed_shotsBooleanShows the path a shot would take while its shooter aims (a drawn bow, ready trident or loaded crossbow) instead of following fired projectiles. Ends at the first block or tracked entity hit and uses projectile_trail. Fireworks aren't predicted.✗false
    aim_charge_colorColorpreview_aimed_shots only. The aim line's color when the draw has just started, shifting to the projectile trail's color as the shot gets ready. Set it to the trail's color to turn the shift off.✗#FFD23F
    entity_trailIdentifierThe Palladium trail (palladium/trails/.json) that draws entity paths. Its renderer, lifetime, offset and spacing set the look.✗argon:path_vision_entity
    projectile_trailIdentifierThe Palladium trail that draws projectile paths, set up like entity_trail so projectiles can look different from entities. Defaults to "argon:path_vision_projectile".✗argon:path_vision_projectile
    trail_render_distanceDouble (4.0 ~ 512.0)Paths of targets farther than this from the camera are not drawn.✗64.0
    trail_smoothingFloat (0.0 ~ 1.0)How much navigation corners are rounded. A rounded stretch that would pass through a block is left sharp instead.✗0.7
    render_through_wallsBooleanWhether the trail can be seen through blocks. Applies to trails drawn with Palladium's laser render types, which includes the gradient and lightning trails.✗false

  ]

    Projectile Effect

    IDargon:projectile_effect
    Shoots a projectile like the built-in projectile ability, and can also give one or more status effects to the living entity it hits.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    entity_typeEntity Type IDID of an entity type (must be a projectile).✓/
    entity_dataNBTAdditional NBT data for the projectile entity.✗/
    inaccuracy(Dynamic) ValueInaccuracy when shooting the projectile. A value, so it can change with conditions (for example a wider spread while overloaded).✗0
    velocityFloat (>= 0.0)Velocity with which the projectile is being shot.✗1.5
    swinging_armnone
    main_arm

    left_arm

    ignore_player_movementBooleanNormally the player's current velocity is added to the projectile's velocity. This turns that off.✗false
    offsetVector 3DA [x, y, z] spawn offset, relative to the entity's facing direction. Defaults to [0, 0, 0].✗(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
    hit_effectsProjectile Hit Effect,
    Projectile Hit Effect[]    		Each entry configures its own effect, duration, amplifier, particles, and powers* (a list of {power, mode} entries, where "power" is an explicit power id, a power tag ("#namespace:tag"), or a mix of both - "include" requires a matching power, "exclude" forbids one) - all entries are granted to whatever living entity the projectile directly hits. Empty by default, meaning no effect is granted.✓/
    item_tintItem TintOnly meaningful for an entity_type whose appearance includes an "item" appearance (e.g. "palladium:custom_projectile"). Tints every such appearance's item using whatever colour a registered source reads off an item in "slot" (a Palladium player slot, e.g. "mainhand", "curios:hands" - every item currently in that slot is checked, and the first one "source" finds a colour on wins), the same way a dyed item is tinted - so this only has a visible effect if the appearance item's own model has a tint-indexed layer to begin with. An id nothing has registered, or no matching item in the slot, silently leaves the appearance untinted; omit "item_tint" entirely for a projectile that should never be tinted.✗/
    max_rangeDoubleIf above 0, the projectile disappears once it has flown this many blocks from where it was shot.✗0
    sprint_interruptInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		If above 0, a living entity the projectile hits cannot sprint for this long.✗0

    Recite

    IDargon:recite
    Says the last spell the user cast, at their current mastery tier, as if typed in chat. Other spell systems can register a recite hook, and whichever system cast most recently is the one recited. If it is a toggle that is already on, it says the stop phrase instead. Cooldown, the spell being unlocked and the voiceless effect still apply.

    Reconstruction

    IDargon:reconstruction
    On activation, matches the item in "target_slot" against "reconstructions" and uses up the first match with enough input to make its result. With "recipe", hold to browse crafting recipes for the held item and release to swap.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    reconstructionsReconstruction Entry[],
    recipe    		The ordered list of input-to-result conversions this ability can perform, or the literal string "recipe" to browse crafting table recipes that use the held item instead. In recipe mode every other ingredient is ignored and only the held item is consumed.✓/
    target_slotmainhand
    offhand
    head
    chest
    legs
    feet
    body
    curios:head
    curios:necklace    		Which slot's item is checked and consumed; defaults to the main hand.✗mainhand
    conversion_modesingle
    maximum
    fixed    		SINGLE applies the matched recipe once, MAXIMUM as many times as the input allows, FIXED up to "fixed_amount" times. Ignored in recipe mode.✗SINGLE
    fixed_amountInteger (> 0)How many times to apply the recipe when conversion_mode is FIXED. Ignored in recipe mode.✗1
    overflow_behaviorfail
    drop    		FAIL cancels the whole conversion if the result can't fully fit in the inventory. DROP inserts what fits and drops the rest at the user's feet.✗FAIL
    component_policyresult_only
    copy_safe
    copy_all    		RESULT_ONLY uses exactly the result's components. COPY_SAFE also copies cosmetic ones (name, lore, dye color, custom model data) from the input. COPY_ALL copies every component that differs from the item's defaults.✗RESULT_ONLY

    reconstructions[] (Reconstruction Entry)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    inputIngredient / ItemThe item or tag that is used up.✓/
    input_amountInteger (> 0)How many of the input are used up.✗1
    resultItem / ItemStackThe item stack that is made.✓/
    result_amountInteger (> 0)Overrides the amount of the result.✗/
    priorityIntegerEntries with a higher priority are checked first.✗0

    {
  "type": "argon:reconstruction",
  "reconstructions": {
    "input": "minecraft:iron_ingot",
    "input_amount": 3,
    "result": {
      "id": "minecraft:iron_pickaxe",

    Reveal

    IDargon:reveal
    While enabled, shows a nametag above every entity within radius, visible only to the ability holder and through walls unless blocked by the block types in blocked_by.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    radius(Dynamic) ValueThe radius, in blocks, within which entities are revealed.✓/
    entitiesliving
    all    		Which entities to reveal, either living entities only (excluding armor stands) or all entities, including non-living ones which only show a name.✗LIVING
    show_nameBooleanWhether to show the entity's name.✗true
    show_healthBooleanWhether to show the entity's current / max health.✗false
    show_powersBooleanWhether to show the entity's Palladium powers, by name.✗false
    show_effectsBooleanWhether to list the entity's active effects with their remaining time.✗false
    filterReveal FilterIf set, only entities that match at least one of these are revealed: their type is in entity_tag, they have any active effect, or they own a matching power.✗/
    look_target_onlyBooleanIf true, only the living entity the user is looking at, within the radius, is revealed.✗false
    hostile_name_colorColorIf set, overrides just the name's color (not health/powers) for hostile entities.✗/
    passive_name_colorColorIf set, overrides just the name's color (not health/powers) for non-hostile entities.✗/
    blocked_byBlock ID(s) / TagIf set, hides a revealed entity's tag when one of these block types blocks the line of sight to the caster's eyes.✗/

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    entity_tagEntity Type TagOnly entities in this tag are revealed.✗/

    powerPower RequirementOnly entities that match this power requirement are revealed.✗/

    Seek Strike

    IDargon:seek_strike
    On activation, picks up to "max_targets" living entities around the user and rushes between them one after another, hitting each once with fixed damage and knockback. Allies are skipped, and a target is skipped when solid blocks are in the way. The user stays beside the last target. All Values are read once on activation.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    range(Dynamic) ValueHow far from the user targets can be chosen, in blocks.✓/
    max_targets(Dynamic) ValueHow many targets are hit at most. Each can only be hit once.✗1
    damage(Dynamic) ValueThe final damage of each hit. The user's attack damage is not added.✓/
    damage_typeDamage Type IDThe damage type used; a player attack when left out.✗/
    knockback(Dynamic) ValueKnockback strength of each hit, where 0.4 is a normal hit.✗0
    lift(Dynamic) ValueUpward velocity added to every hit target.✗0.2
    speedDoubleHow many blocks per tick the user travels towards a target.✗2.5
    reachDoubleHow close, in blocks, the user gets to a target before striking.✗1.8
    aimlook
    nearest
    marked    		"look" picks the entity under the crosshair first, otherwise the nearest one inside cone_angle. "nearest" starts from the entity closest to the user. "marked" only goes for the user's argon:target_mark target (hostile_only is ignored, and nothing happens without a mark).✗look
    cone_angleDoubleThe full opening angle of the look cone, in degrees.✗90.0
    hostile_onlyBooleanIf true, only hostile mobs and other players can be picked.✗true
    end_effectsPotion Hit Effect,
    Potion Hit Effect[]    		Effects applied to the user after the last hit, for example a short slowdown.✗[]
    hit_visualsBeam Visual[]Particle visuals spawned at each target when it is hit, in the same format as the visuals of argon:energy_beam.✗[]
    travel_visualsBeam Visual[]Particle visuals spawned along every step of the rush, for example a streak.✗[]
    hit_soundIdentifierA sound event played at every target when it is hit, instead of the default hit sound.✗/
    hit_sound_volumeFloatVolume of hit_sound.✗1.0
    hit_sound_pitchFloatPitch of hit_sound.✗0.9
    hit_effectsPotion Hit Effect,
    Potion Hit Effect[]    		Effects applied to every target that is hit, for example a short slowdown that interrupts its movement.✗[]
    consume_markBooleanIf true, a hit on the user's marked target ends the mark.✗false
    execute_thresholdDoubleA target at or below this health fraction (0 to 1) takes execute_bonus extra damage. 0 disables it.✗0.0
    execute_bonus(Dynamic) ValueThe extra damage dealt to a target under execute_threshold.✗0
    dashBooleanIf true and no target was chosen, the user dashes straight along the look direction for up to range blocks (stopping at walls) and strikes the first valid entity it touches. Not used with aim marked.✗false
    exit_speedDoubleSpeed in blocks per tick the user keeps along the last movement direction when the rush ends, instead of stopping dead.✗0.0

    end_effects (Potion Hit Effect)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    effectMob Effect IDThe effect to apply.✓/
    durationInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long the effect lasts.✓/
    amplifierIntegerThe effect level, starting at 0.✗/
    max_amplifierIntegerThe highest level repeated hits can stack the effect up to.✗/
    particlesBooleanWhether the effect shows its particles.✗/

    hit_visuals[] (Beam Visual)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    shapestreak
    helix
    ring
    sphere
    burst
    crescent    		The particle pattern to draw.✓/
    anchorend
    caster    		Whether the pattern is drawn at the end of the beam or around the caster.✗/
    orientationhorizontal
    vertical    		How ring and crescent patterns are turned.✗/
    particleParticleThe particle used.✓/
    countInteger (1 ~ 512)How many particles the pattern uses.✗/
    radiusFloat (0.0 ~ 64.0)The radius of the pattern in blocks.✗/
    stepFloat (0.05 ~ 16.0)The spacing between particles along the beam.✗/
    pitchFloat (0.1 ~ 64.0)The length of one full twist for helixes, in blocks.✗/
    strandsInteger (1 ~ 8)How many strands a helix has.✗/
    arcFloat (1.0 ~ 360.0)How much of a circle is drawn, in degrees.✗/
    heightFloatThe height of the pattern in blocks.✗/
    ringsInteger (1 ~ 16)How many rings are drawn.✗/
    speedDoubleThe speed of the particles.✗/
    spreadFloat (0.0 ~ 8.0)How far the particles scatter.✗/

    State Selector

    IDargon:state_selector
    On activation, changes a block state property (e.g. "open", "lit", "facing") of the block you target, using "block_properties". With several entries, a held key scrolls a menu of the ones that apply.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    rangeInteger (> 0)The maximum distance, in blocks, the raycast can reach.✗8
    block_filterBlock ID(s) / TagOptional whitelist of blocks (explicit IDs and/or tags) this ability can affect; if unset, any block is eligible.✗/
    block_propertiesState Selector Property,
    State Selector Property[]    		One or more properties to offer. A single entry applies immediately. Several entries open a scrollable picker.✓/
    allow_block_entitiesBooleanIf false (default), refuses to touch any block with a block entity (chests, furnaces, etc.) for safety.✗false
    notify_neighborsBooleanIf true (default), the change triggers normal neighbor updates (redstone, shape updates, etc). The client is always synced either way.✗true
    require_valid_survivalBooleanIf true (default), the new state must be able to survive at that position or the change is cancelled.✗true
    allow_multiblockBooleanIf false (default), won't change structural multi-block properties ("half", "part", e.g. doors, beds, tall plants), since one half alone can desync the pair. Modded blocks with other names aren't all covered, use "block_filter" for those.✗false

    block_properties (State Selector Property)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    propertyStringThe name of the block state property, such as open, facing or waterlogged. Whatever the targeted block actually has is used.✓/
    operationset
    next
    previous
    toggle    		How the property changes.✓/
    valueStringThe value used by the set operation, in its normal string form such as true, east or 3.✗/
    allowed_valuesString,
    String[]    		Restricts and orders the values this property may use.✗[]

    Takeoff

    IDargon:charged_takeoff
    Hold the Takeoff key (Controls > Argon, unbound by default) to charge, release to launch. The longer you hold, the harder it throws you. One push, not flight. Pair it with argon:took_off to continue into flight.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    requires_groundBooleanWhether charging can only begin on the ground (checked on the server).✗true
    cancel_when_airborneBooleanWhether a charge started on the ground is dropped once the player leaves it (walking off a ledge, jumping).✗true
    allow_movement_while_chargingBooleanWhether the player can walk while charging. If false, walking speed is held at zero until they release or cancel.✗true
    min_charge_timeInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long the key must be held before releasing launches. Releasing sooner cancels, with no launch and no cooldown.✗4
    max_charge_timeInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long a full charge takes. Holding longer adds nothing, they stay fully charged until release.✗40
    cooldownInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long after a launch before another can be charged. 0 for none. Cancelled charges don't start it.✗0
    min_launch_strengthDoubleUpward speed, in blocks per tick, of the weakest launch (a normal jump is about 0.42). 0.6 gets roughly 2.7 blocks.✗0.6
    max_launch_strengthDoubleUpward speed of a full charge, never exceeded. 1.7 gets roughly 15 blocks before gravity wins.✗1.7
    flight_at_apexBooleanStarts the player's palladium:flight at the top of the climb so they stay up. Needs an unlocked flight ability, does nothing without one.✗false
    launch_directionvertical
    look_direction
    hybrid    		Which way the push goes: "vertical" (straight up), "look_direction" (where the player looks on release, same strength at any angle) or "hybrid" (up, bent toward the look direction by "directional_influence").✗vertical
    minimum_launch_pitchDoublelook_direction only. The lowest launch angle, in degrees above the horizon (negative is below). 0 never launches downward, -90 means no limit.✗-90.0
    directional_influenceDoublehybrid only. 0 to 1, how much the look direction bends the launch away from straight up. Strongest looking level, nothing looking straight up or down. It never changes how hard the launch is, only where it points.✗0.35
    minimum_upward_componentDoublehybrid only. 0 to 1, the least vertical share the launch may have, whatever the camera does. 0.5 keeps at least half the push pointing up, 1 is straight up.✗0.5
    directional_launch_particlesBooleanWhether the burst of debris at launch is thrown away from the launch direction (backward for a forward launch) instead of spreading around the player.✗false
    replace_velocityBooleanWhether the push replaces the player's whole velocity. By default sideways speed is kept (never raised above what they had or max_launch_strength), so launches can't be chained into unlimited speed.✗false
    charge_curvelinear
    ease_in
    ease_out

    Target Mark

    IDargon:target_mark
    On activation, marks the living entity under the crosshair (or the closest one inside the cone) as the user's prey. Only one mark exists per user and a new mark replaces the old one. While marked, the target is outlined through walls for the user, an edge arrow points at it when it is off screen, and every hit the user lands on it deals extra damage. The mark ends when the duration runs out, the target dies, or something consumes it (see argon:seek_strike). Use the argon:marked_target condition to build abilities that need a mark. All Values are read once on activation.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    range(Dynamic) ValueHow far away a target can be marked, in blocks.✗32
    duration(Dynamic) ValueHow long the mark lasts, in ticks.✗300
    damage_bonus(Dynamic) ValueExtra damage the user deals to the marked target, in percent.✗10
    colorColorThe outline and arrow color of the mark.✗#F2C451
    cone_angleDoubleThe full opening angle of the fallback cone used when no entity is directly under the crosshair, in degrees.✗24.0
    pointerBooleanWhether an arrow at the screen edge points at the marked target when it is off screen.✗true

  "type": "argon:target_mark",
  "range": 32,
  "duration": 300,
  "damage_bonus": 10,
  "properties": {
    "title": "Target Mark"
  }
}

    Tentacle Guard

    IDargon:appendage_guard
    While enabled, idle appendages wrap around your torso and absorb damage from within "block_angle" of where you face, up to "guard_threshold". Past that the guard breaks, you take the damage and can't block for "break_lockout" ticks.

    minimum_wrapped_appendagesIntegerHow many appendages must stay wrapped for the guard to absorb damage. Below this, hits go through.✗2
    maximum_wrapped_appendagesIntegerHow many appendages this ability claims and wraps at once.✗4
    guard_thresholdFloatCumulative damage the guard can absorb before it breaks.✗20.0
    break_damageFloatSelf-damage dealt to the wearer when the guard breaks.✗2.0
    break_lockoutIntegerTicks after breaking before guard can absorb damage again.✗40
    block_angleFloatThe cone, in degrees around your facing, that damage must come from to be blocked. Also how wide the appendages spread around you. 180 (default) covers the front, 360 covers every direction.✗180.0
    knockback_strengthFloatKnockback velocity applied to the attacker on a successful block.✗0.3

    Time Growth

    IDargon:time_growth
    Makes attributes grow stronger the longer the ability has been enabled for the player. Every enabled tick counts towards the ability's age (time spent offline or with the ability disabled does not count), and each entry adds "per_day" to its attribute for every day of age between "start_day" and "max_day". The age is available to other abilities through the argon:power_age value and condition.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    attributesGrowth Entry[]The attributes that grow, from 1 to 32 entries.✓/
    ticks_per_dayIntegerHow many enabled ticks count as one day of age. 24000 is one Minecraft day, lower it to test growth quickly.✗24000
    whole_daysBooleanIf true the bonus only increases once per full day. If false it grows smoothly.✗true
    reset_on_deathBooleanIf true the age goes back to 0 when the player dies.✗true
    reset_on_power_lossBooleanIf true the age goes back to 0 when the player loses the power this ability belongs to.✗true
    milestonesGrowth Milestone[]Ages that announce themselves when the player reaches them by natural growth. They do not fire when the age is set with a command.✗[]

    attributes[] (Growth Entry)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    attributeAttribute IDThe attribute that grows.✓/
    operationadd_value
    add_multiplied_base
    add_multiplied_total    		How the bonus is applied to the attribute.✗add_value
