    Wall Crawling

    IDargon:wall_crawling
    Lets the user climb flat vertical walls and optionally ceilings with look-relative WASD. Turns around outside corners on its own and rolls the camera so the attached surface reads as "down".

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    base_speedFloatThe base crawling speed, in blocks per tick, before speed_multiplier is applied.✗0.13
    speed_multiplierFloatMultiplies base_speed, so different powers can reuse this ability at different crawl speeds (0.5 is half speed, 2.0 is double).✗1.0
    attach_distanceFloatHow close to a wall or ceiling face the user must be to attach to (or remain attached to) it.✗0.5
    detach_strengthFloatHow hard jumping off a surface pushes the user in whichever direction they're currently looking.✗0.3
    gravity_pull_strengthFloatA small constant velocity into the attached surface every tick, whether or not the user is moving. The same solid block collision that stops it confirms the surface is still there, so there is no distance check.✗0.08
    ceiling_crawlingBooleanWhether ceilings (not just vertical walls) are valid attachment surfaces.✗true
    camera_rollBooleanIf true, smoothly rolls the local user's camera so the attached surface reads as "down", making the wall or ceiling their floor and not just their movement plane.✗true
    third_person_camera_rollBooleanWhether camera_roll also applies in third person, not only first person. Off by default, since third person shows the user's own model and the roll doesn't reorient it.✗false
    use_directional_gravityBooleanIf true, attaching to a surface turns the player's gravity toward it (the surface becomes their floor, and the hitbox, camera and model turn with it) instead of steering velocity along it. The options below apply to this mode.✗false
    gravity_strengthFloatA multiplier on normal gravity while attached; it is how firmly the player is held to the surface.✗1.0
    rotate_cameraBooleanWhether the camera turns with the surface. If missing, camera_roll is used. When false the view stays upright to the world while the body and movement still turn.✗/
    camera_transition_timeIntegerTicks the camera takes to turn to a new surface. 0 turns it at once.✗6
    smooth_transitionsBooleanWhether the camera and body turn gradually. When false every turn is instant.✗true
    transition_durationIntegerTicks the drawn body takes to turn to a new surface.✗6
    transition_easingStringlinear, ease_in, ease_out or ease_in_out: how the turns speed up and slow down.✗ease_in_out
    view_orientationStringWhat a turn between surfaces does to where the player looks. relative: same angles in the new gravity. world: angles are recomputed so the player keeps looking at the same point in the world.✗relative
    surface_detection_rangeFloatHow close a surface must be to grab or keep hold of it, in blocks. If missing, attach_distance is used.✗/
    surface_transition_toleranceFloatHow far before the edge of a surface the player starts turning round it, in blocks (0 to 0.3).✗0.15
    movement_modeStringsurface_relative: W goes up the wall (or along the heading) whatever the camera does. camera_relative: W goes where the camera points, along the surface.✗surface_relative
    surface_jump_strengthFloatHow hard jumping pushes the player straight off the surface. If missing, detach_strength is used.✗/
    auto_crawlBooleanWhether the player may turn onto surfaces where only a crawl sized body fits, crawling through tight spaces.✗true
    allow_ceiling_crawlingBooleanWhether ceilings are valid surfaces. If missing, ceiling_crawling is used.✗/
    allow_corner_transitionsBooleanWhether the player turns from one surface to the next at corners on their own (and from the floor onto a wall they walk into). When false they can only grab a surface from the air.✗true
    preserve_surface_momentumBooleanWhether speed is kept through a turn between surfaces.✗true
    surface_speed_multiplierFloatMultiplies the crawling speed (base_speed times speed_multiplier) on a surface only.✗1.0
    allow_surface_sprintingBooleanWhether sprinting makes the player crawl faster.✗true
    crawl_when_not_sprintingBooleanIf true, the player is crawl sized (the vanilla crawling pose, a 0.6 block hitbox that fits one block gaps) on a wall or ceiling unless sprinting. Sprinting stands them back up as far as there is room.✗false
    play_running_animationBooleanWhether sprinting along a wall or ceiling plays the running animation. Vanilla only starts it from ground movement, which doesn't happen while climbing. Only while sprinting.✗true

    {
  "type": "argon:wall_crawling",
  "properties": {
    "title": "Wall Crawling"
  }
}

    Web Swing

    IDargon:web_swing
    On activation, attaches a rope anchor and swings you like a pendulum while enabled. The rope only cancels motion past its length, turning momentum into an arc. Movement keys steer. Ends on disable, or optionally on ground contact or lost line of sight.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    rangeDoubleThe maximum distance an anchor can attach to, measured from the eye to the exact hit point.✓/
    attach_toblock
    entity
    both    		Which kind of raycast hit can be attached to: a fixed "block" anchor, a "entity" living entity that becomes a moving anchor followed for the rest of the swing, or "both" (whichever the raycast hits first).✗BOTH
    beam_rendererIdentifierThe id of the beam renderer used to draw the rope from the user to the anchor point.✓/
    initial_slackFloatExtra rope length, in blocks, on top of the exact distance when the web attaches. 0 (default) starts the rope as long as the current distance, so attaching never snaps or stalls you. Raise it for a more dramatic catch.✗0.0
    gravity_multiplierFloatScales gravity's pull while swinging. 1 (default) is normal gravity. Other values adjust vanilla's gravity rather than replace it.✗1.0
    pump_accelerationFloatAcceleration, blocks/tick^2, from holding forward or back along the rope's tangent plane. It fades out as speed nears max_speed and stops below a minimum speed so you can't hover. 0 is momentum only.✗0.025
    air_dragFloatExtra multiplier on velocity every tick while swinging, 0 to 1. 1 (default) keeps momentum (vanilla's own air drag is already undone, see drag_compensation).✗1.0
    handright
    left    		Which hand the web comes from (drives left/right animation mirroring). Defaults to left if the beam_renderer id ends in "left", otherwise right.✗/
    auto_tightenBooleanSlowly takes slack out of the rope (never pulling the user, and never below their current distance plus rope_slack_tolerance), so a swing that goes slack gets a usable rope again instead of the web quietly failing.✗true
    rope_reel_speedFloatHow fast auto_tighten removes slack, blocks/tick.✗0.12
    minimum_rope_lengthFloatAuto-tightening never shortens the rope below this length, blocks.✗3.0
    rope_slack_toleranceFloatHow much slack, blocks, auto_tighten leaves in the rope.✗0.6
    max_rope_correctionFloatThe most, in blocks per tick, the rope may move the user back onto its radius after an overshoot, so a correction is paid off gradually instead of as a snap.✗1.0
    drag_compensationBooleanUndo vanilla's per-tick air drag (x0.91 horizontal, x0.98 vertical) while swinging in the air, so a swing keeps its momentum. Turn it off only to compare against plain vanilla drag.✗true
    max_speedFloatCaps the user's total speed, blocks/tick, while swinging. Defaults to 2.6; 0 removes the cap.✗/
    slack_visual_scaleFloatHow far the rope must sag, as a fraction of its length, before the beam looks fully loose. Only beam renderers like argon:segmented_textured use it, and only on the swinging player's client. Everyone else sees a taut web.✗0.5
    reelWeb Swing ReelIf present, holding jump reels the rope in and holding sneak reels it back out (up to the original attach length), both at "speed" blocks/tick, down to "min_length" blocks at the shortest. Leave unset (the default) to disable manual reeling.✗/
    auto_releaseWeb Swing Auto ReleaseWhich conditions automatically detach the rope: "on_ground" when the user touches the ground, and "on_blocked_line" when a solid block ends up blocking the straight line between the user and the anchor point. Both default to true.✗AutoReleaseSettings[onGround=true, onBlockedLine=true]
    swing_assistWeb Swing AssistTargeting and assist tuning. Targeting is a direct raycast along the aim first (a valid hit always wins); only if that misses, or hits closer than "min_anchor_distance", a small cone of "anchor_cone_degrees" (default 10) is searched, with aim accuracy weighted far above "anchor_height_weight" (default 0.4, the most a high target can gain over an on-aim one). "velocity_blend_speed" (default 0 = off) blends the travel direction into the aim direction. "ground_clearance_strength" (default 0.5) softens downward speed just before grazing the ground. "lateral_steering_strength" (default 0.02) is the left/right equivalent of pump_acceleration. "swing_jump_strength" (default 0 = pure momentum release) is an optional boost applied if jump is held on release. "fall_damage_grace_ticks" (default 15) forgives fall damage for that long after release. "rope_wrap" (default true) lets the rope catch on the nearest obstruction between the anchor and the user.✗SwingAssistSettings[anchorConeDegrees=10.0, minAnchorDistance=3.0, anchorHeightWeight=0.4, velocityBlendSpeed=0.0, groundClearanceStrength=0.5, lateralSteeringStrength=0.02, swingJumpStrength=0.0, fallDamageGraceTicks=15, ropeWrap=true]

    reel (Web Swing Reel)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    speedFloat (>= 0.0)How fast the line reels in.✗/
    min_lengthFloatThe shortest the line can get, in blocks.✗/

    auto_release (Web Swing Auto Release)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    on_groundBooleanRelease the line when the user lands.✗/
    on_blocked_lineBooleanRelease the line when something blocks it.✗/

    swing_assist (Web Swing Assist)

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    anchor_cone_degreesFloat (0.0 ~ 45.0)How far from the crosshair an anchor can be and still be picked, in degrees.✗10.0
    min_anchor_distanceFloat (>= 0.0)The closest an anchor can be, in blocks.✗/
    anchor_height_weightFloat (>= 0.0)How much higher anchors are preferred.✗/
    velocity_blend_speedFloat (>= 0.0)How quickly the swing direction follows the user's movement.✗/
    ground_clearance_strengthFloat (0.0 ~ 1.0)How strongly the swing lifts the user away from the ground.✗/
    lateral_steering_strengthFloat (>= 0.0)How strongly the user can steer sideways while swinging.✗/
    swing_jump_strengthFloat (>= 0.0)How strong the jump off the line is.✗/
    fall_damage_grace_ticksInteger (>= 0)For this many ticks after releasing, fall damage is ignored.✗/
    rope_wrapBooleanWhether the line wraps around corners.✗/

    Zone

    IDargon:zone
    On its first enabled tick, makes a circle on the ground at the user or where they look. Every interval it damages enemies inside and applies effects to them and allies, and allies take less damage. Ends when time is up or the user strays too far.

    radius(Dynamic) ValueThe radius of the circle in blocks, read once when it is created.✓/
    durationInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How long the zone lasts.✗100
    look_target_rangeDoubleIf set, the zone is created where the user looks, up to this many blocks away, instead of at the user.✗/
    intervalInteger,
    Time String ("40s", "2m", etc.)    		How often damage and effects are applied.✗20
    damage(Dynamic) ValueDamage dealt to each enemy on every interval.✗0
    damage_typeDamage Type IDThe damage type used; the user's normal attack when left out.✗/
    effectsBeam Effect[]Effects applied to enemies on every interval.✗/
    ally_effectsBeam Effect[]Effects applied to the user, their team and their pets on every interval.✗/
    ally_damage_reduction(Dynamic) ValueThe fraction from 0 to 1 of damage the user, their team and their pets do not take while inside. A Value read once when the zone is created, so it can scale with power age.✗0.0
    follow_userBooleanIf true, the zone moves with the user instead of staying where it was created.✗false
    reduction_affects_userBooleanIf false, the damage reduction applies only to allies, not the user (useful when the user has their own reduction).✗true
    end_with_abilityBooleanIf true, the zone ends as soon as this ability is no longer enabled.✗false
    end_beyondDoubleIf set, the zone ends when the user is farther than this many blocks from its centre.✗/
    particleParticleA particle drawn around the edge of the zone.✗/

    Zoom

    IDargon:zoom
    While enabled, zooms your view to the magnification in "zoom" and eases back out when disabled. It follows "zoom" as it changes, so a data attachment can let scrolling adjust it. Only affects your own view.

    KeyTypeDescriptionRequiredFallback
    zoom(Dynamic) ValueThe magnification: 1 is normal, 2 is twice the size, 4 four times. A value, so a data attachment can change it while zoomed. Below 1 counts as 1, 100 is the max. With "level_factor" above 1 it is a level instead.✗2.0
    rateDoubleHow quickly the view closes on the magnification, per second, when zooming and when "zoom" changes. Higher is snappier. 6 covers about 63% of the way in a sixth of a second.✗6.0
    level_factorDouble1 (default) means "zoom" is the magnification. Above 1, "zoom" is a level and the magnification is level_factor raised to it, so every scroll step changes the view by the same proportion.✗1.0
    scale_sensitivityBooleanWhether turning the camera slows down as the view zooms in, so aiming stays steady (like a spyglass). At 4x the camera turns a quarter as far for the same mouse movement.✗true
    scale_render_distanceBooleanWhether draw distances grow with the zoom so magnified things stay visible: block entities, other entities, sign outlines and name tags. Only already loaded terrain can show.✗true
    reset_on_disableBooleanWhether turning the zoom off puts the level back to "base_level" (in "level_attachment"), so the next zoom starts from the base instead of wherever it was scrolled to. Needs "level_attachment".✗false
    level_attachmentData Attachment IDThe number data attachment that holds the zoom level (the one "zoom" reads and scrolling changes), which "reset_on_disable" sets back to "base_level". Only used by "reset_on_disable".✗none
    base_levelIntegerThe value "reset_on_disable" sets the level attachment to.✗0

    {
  "type": "argon:zoom",
  "zoom": 4,
  "rate": 8,
  "reset_on_disable": true,

    "title": "Zoom"
  }
}
